newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese bureaucrats told to refuse lecture fees.
newsitem.headline: Japanese bureaucrats told to refuse lecture fees.

text.p: Bureaucrats at Japan's Finance Ministry, much in demand as speakers at lecture meetings, are being told not to take payments for such appearances.
"The request has been made to each bureau in the ministry in view of scandals involving ministry officials and mounting public criticism of the ministry," a ministry official told Reuters on Friday.
Financial sources said senior ministry officials are offered handsome payments for such appearances, sometimes amounting to several thousand dollars.
Banks and securities firms use such lecture meetings as a chance to strengthen relations with the ministry and get detailed information about ministry measures.
"I am afraid that not many ministry officials now accept invitations to meetings without any payments," said an official at an institution which organises lecture meetings.

The ministry, long viewed as the pinnacle of Japan's elite bureaucracy, has come under fierce public criticism for its poor handling of problems in the financial sector and its close links with the business world.
Finance Minister Wataru Kubo last week apologised for the involvement of a retired ministry official in trading in shares in a consumer finance firm before it went public.
In September 1995, then-finance minister Masayoshi Takemura docked his own pay over a scandal in which a senior ministry official took improper payments from business contacts.
Politicians have stepped up pressure to streamline the ministry's functions in order to curb its authority.
